title: Find the First Event at or After a Timestamp
real_world_story: A monitoring system stores event timestamps in sorted order. When an operator enters a timestamp, the system needs to quickly locate the first event that occurred at that time or after it.

real_world_connection.system: Time-indexed event and log monitoring system
real_world_connection.target_represents: The earliest event timestamp that is greater than or equal to the requested timestamp
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Using binary search to quickly locate a lower-bound position in sorted event data

problem_statement: Given a sorted array of event timestamps and a target timestamp, find the index of the first timestamp that is greater than or equal to the target. If no such timestamp exists, print -1.
task: Search the sorted event timestamps and return the zero-based index of the first timestamp greater than or equal to the target.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of recorded events. The second line contains N space-separated timestamps in non-decreasing order. The third line contains the target timestamp.
output_format: Print the zero-based index of the first timestamp greater than or equal to the target. If no such timestamp exists, print -1.
constraints: Timestamps are sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: The first timestamp greater than or equal to 35 is 40 at index 3.
There is no timestamp greater than or equal to 60.

expected_algorithm.name: Binary Search
expected_algorithm.reason: The event timestamps are sorted, allowing binary search to locate the required timestamp position in logarithmic time.

hint: Maintain low and high boundaries for the search range.
If the middle timestamp is greater than or equal to the target, store it and search the left half.
real_world_takeaway: Binary search enables monitoring systems to quickly locate events in large time-indexed logs without scanning every recorded event.
